<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/tool.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via PACKAGE_SLOTTED_STORE_TYPES (symbol, a top-level const object))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/tool.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **183** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5b2ec820c8abca113eae23745f71331f55ec7aed` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9210f1fa94ecf642a8288811f048ae5ca00b2971` — the merge of head `6b16ccaa9a4f9659c08ea11ff32161fc818fbe7c` into base `5b2ec820c8abca113eae23745f71331f55ec7aed`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9210f1fa94ecf642a8288811f048ae5ca00b2971 && git checkout 9210f1fa94ecf642a8288811f048ae5ca00b2971
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5b2ec820c8abca113eae23745f71331f55ec7aed 6b16ccaa9a4f9659c08ea11ff32161fc818fbe7c && git checkout -B drift-repro 5b2ec820c8abca113eae23745f71331f55ec7aed && git merge --no-ff 6b16ccaa9a4f9659c08ea11ff32161fc818fbe7c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5b2ec820c8abca113eae23745f71331f55ec7aed
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5b2ec820c8abca113eae23745f71331f55ec7aed` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

This record is their delta on the new head, routed here by triage (6857847759). Everything the two earlier records judged and the interdiff does not touch stands as read there. The red-line re-read is the epic seat's and is not this record.

### ① Derived judgments

- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is right, with both arms as written: the install door, the item seam and the boot seal accept a second holder from another namespace, and the metadata service's in-process answers for a tool move from served to refused or empty.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` is right: an author may now ship a tool under a name a package of another namespace already holds. No key or value is refused that was accepted.
- The production change is still two set memberships and docblocks. Every reader of the two sets is a membership test; none keeps a per-type table that `tool` would have to join.
- The merge of `main` moves no answer of this PR. Its four conflicts with the webhook narrowing are unions: both types stay in both sets, in both module docblocks and in the plural-read pin.
- The second changeset's `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right: the semantic entry adds no key and no export.

### ② Semver level

- `minor` on `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/metadata`, the `!` title and the BREAKING banner: unchanged and right for `added` with a narrowing arm.
- `adr-0087: registered tool-names-per-namespace` replaces the not-required marker, as the red-line read ruled. The entry file is found by directory, has the five fields, and its remedy names calls that exist (`unregisterPackage`, `migrateDatabaseLoaderRowPackages` and its three left-row reasons).
- `patch` on `@objectstack/spec` for the entry follows the upgrade-guide entries already in `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head, all concluded: 67 runs, 55 success, 11 skipped, 1 failure. The failure is `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)`, from the 15:45Z run and not run again since. It reads the PR body and the card, not the diff, so no judgment in this record rests on it. The report on the card expects its duplicate leg to stay red while #32895 was open; #32895 closed at 15:51Z, after that run. Which leg failed was not read here. Every build, type, lint and test check of the diff is green. The guard is the seat's before ACCEPT: it runs again on a body edit or a re-run.
- File surface. Claim 6855871184 lists the three production files, the objectql tests, `tool.json`, the ADR-0087 entry and `.changeset/**`. Outside that text: the dogfood pin (asked for by ruling 3), the two metadata tests, the CLI integration test and the ADR anchor file. All but the dogfood edit and the plural-read line come from the earlier head. The seat names it at ACCEPT.
- `Skills-docs:` reads `#32916 (owed: …) — otherwise …`; the form is `follow-up #32916`. #32916 is open, `pm:blocked`, p3. The seat's.
- Rulings 4 and 5 of the red-line read are carried to the seat by the report: #32914 is cited from the red-line read's scratch merge and was not run again, and the card widening #32692's second case is not filed yet. Not read here.
- The two set-membership ablations were not repeated on this head; the report gives the reason (the merge moved neither entry). The ablation of the sealed-type rule is the report's, not run here.
- `main` is five commits past the merge base, none on a path of this diff.
- Release: the card was lowered to p2 and taken off the 18.4.0 line (6840298518). The slot is the seat's and the maintainer's.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts`, `packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts`. Unchanged in substance since `d39ba131`: `tool` in both sets, and docblocks that now name `webhook` and `tool` side by side. The two sets still move in one change, as the store's own rule requires.

`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.tool-names-per-namespace.ts` (red-line must-fix 3, ruling 1). Done. `surface` names the five in-process answers and the legacy loader row; `replacement` names the holder by package, by `?package=` or by the qualified address; `reason` gives FROM and TO for each; `acceptanceCriteria` can be checked on a deployment. It says nothing the changeset does not.

`.changeset/31985-tool-names-per-namespace.md` (must-fix 1 and 2, as declarations). Done. Carried path (i) is restated to what `main` does since #32741: a package-less tool row is grafted onto no holder's slot. The two by-order paths that remain are named as older than this PR (two stored rows each naming a holder; the in-process layered read with no service copy). `GET /meta/tool` is no longer listed as moved.

`packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts` (ruling 3, unit). Done. `tool` joins the sealed-type loop: two holders in both registration orders across the four states, and the one-holder case. Each exact address must serve its own on the plain and the layered read, which is the rule and nothing else. The CONTROL that used `tool` as the type not narrowed now uses `dashboard`, a type no one-holder rule covers, so it still controls.

`packages/qa/dogfood/test/bare-name-one-holder-ai-family.dogfood.test.ts` (ruling 3, booted). Done. A package-less row is saved through the real door before two namespaces install the name, one name in id order and one in reverse; each exact address, plain and layered, is read before and after the read-side hydrator, and the bare read must refuse naming both. Not run here.

`packages/spec/liveness/tool.json`. The note's date only.

Findings:

- **n1 nit.** The same describe has two more loops over the sealed types that still list `action` and `queue` only: the service copy of the package-less row, and one holder disabled while the hydrator runs. Ruling 3 did not ask for them, and the rule they pin reads no type. Adding `tool` there is one word each.
- **n2 nit.** Row 16 of the PR table (the in-process layered read on an artifact boot now answers `409` naming both) is a move, labelled narrowing. In the changeset it sits under "Not moved by this change, and carried", outside the BREAKING list, and it has no pin of its own (the PR says it follows row 5, measured by the red-line read). Move the sentence under "Also moved". Changeset prose only.
- **n3 nit.** The `Skills-docs:` form, as flagged in ③.

No must-fix and no should-fix. Must-fix 1 to 3 and ruling 3 of the red-line read 6840825374 are answered on this head; whether they are answered to the epic's red lines is the epic seat's re-read.

### (4) What changed since 6840825374

- **The union with webhook #32577** (merged as `e55347d21`). Both sets now hold `webhook` and `tool`. Both docblocks are kept, and the plural-read pin lists both. I read the conflict resolution with `git show --cc c84542096`.
